subject: Request: Transitional revenue bridge for delayed multi-model routing
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@stratushealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Launch impact & request for commercial bridge

Hi Kimberly —

Quick summary: Stratus is blocked from going live with our major payer-integrations pilot because the multi-model routing feature (pinning variant per customer) isn’t available in time for their go/no-go on 5/10. We surfaced this to the executive sponsor — they are very pragmatic but the delay means additional infra costs for their staging runs and a pushed revenue milestone.

What we need from Redwood: a temporary commercial bridge (either credits or a time-limited discount) to offset the launch costs and keep the project on track while we wait for the feature roll. We’re estimating ~$28k in incremental infra/tests for the next 6 weeks; they’ve asked if Redwood can cover a portion while we finish validation.

Attached: launch_impact_summary.pdf (screenshots, timeline, internal ops cost calc).

Can you escalate for an exec-level concession + formal wording? They want a simple one-page note they can show their CFO.

Thanks — really appreciate any help to keep this pilot live.

— Elena
Elena Morris
VP, Partnerships
Stratus Health

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Launch impact & request for commercial bridge

Team — forwarding Stratus’ ask (attached). High level: customer launch at risk because multi-model routing won’t be ready in time for their 5/10 pilot gate. They’re asking Redwood for a short-term commercial bridge to absorb staging/test infra and keep momentum.

Proposed internal path:
- Produce an interim offer (credit or % discount) limited to the next 6 weeks or until feature shipping, whichever comes first.
- Finance: give me a quick calc for a conservative credit (I put $20k as a starting point in the attached SLA_makegood_calc.xlsx).
- Product (Karthik): can you confirm ETA and whether a targeted rollout to Stratus is possible as an alternative? Also confirm whether any workaround would materially reduce their costs.
- Sales (Ben/Marissa): agree on commercial ask language and whether we should require a short-term commitment in exchange (e.g., 6mo revenue commitment or onboarding milestone).
- Legal: if we give provisional credit, we need simple T&Cs (time-limited, non-precedent). Laura, can you draft a one-paragraph clause?

I think this is an exec-signoff item if the credit is >$15k. Please reply with a short yes/no and a number recommendation; I’ll draft the note to the customer and route to ops leadership for approval.

Attachment: SLA_makegood_calc.xlsx

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Launch impact & request for commercial bridge

Kim / team — thanks for surfacing. Quick product context:
- Root cause: multi-model routing depends on the per-tenant routing table and a small scheduler change; we hit a regression during validation that added 2 weeks to our canary plan. Current ETA for a safe, tested rollout to a single customer is 5/17 (we can accelerate to 5/13 with a manual cutover and extra engineering overhead).
- Workaround: we can provide a temporary pinned-model deployment per customer (manual config) that will reduce their staging infra by ~40%, but that requires a small runbook and run-of-day support from our infra team.

Recommendation:
- Offer a conditional bridge that covers 50% of their documented incremental infra/test cost for up to 4 weeks OR until we put them on the manual pinned deployment (whichever comes first). I ran a quick calc; that’s roughly $14k on the customer numbers in Elena’s doc.
- If we must cover the full 6-week window, cap at a fixed $20k credit and require a short-term commitment (pilot conversion clause).

Constraints: any amount > $15k needs ops/executive approval due to precedent risk. If we go the manual pinned route, we also need a limited support SLA and an ops runbook (I’ll attached prod_timeline_notes.md with steps).

I’m fine with the conditional 50% bridge + manual pinned plan. Will join the customer call if Kim wants me on for the technical explanation.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Lead Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Elena Morris <elena.morris@stratushealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T17:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Launch impact & request for commercial bridge

Looping back after run with Finance: I support the conditional bridge. Finance tentatively okays a single one-time credit of $20,000 (non-recurring) to cover up to 6 weeks of documented incremental infra/test cost, with the following commercial guardrails:
- Credit is time-boxed (expires 60 days after issuance).
- Applies only to costs documented in Stratus’ impact summary and subject to verification.
- Requires a short-term conversion commitment: if Stratus converts the pilot to a paid account within 90 days, Redwood will apply a 10% implementation discount on first quarter committed spend (no retroactive credits).

Kim — I drafted the customer-facing language below; if you and Legal sign off I’ll send it to Elena. If this is >$15k we should route to Ops VP for formal exec signoff (Laura / Kim, can you confirm who approves this in our current approval matrix?).

DRAFT TO CUSTOMER:
Hi Elena — thanks for the note and for the clear impact doc. We’re committed to keeping the pilot on track. As discussed, Redwood will provide a one-time commercial bridge credit of $20,000 to offset documented incremental staging and test costs related to the delayed multi-model routing feature. This credit is conditional on verification of the documented costs and will be applied to your account within 30 days of agreement signature. The credit expires 60 days after issuance. In exchange, we request a short-term pilot-to-paid conversion agreement (90 days) as described below.

Please confirm and we’ll route for internal exec approvals + formal paperwork.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachment: none (calc already shared)
